text: Good API design makes software easy to use and maintain. When building REST APIs, developers should create clear endpoints that represent resources, such as /users or /orders. Each endpoint should use the correct HTTP methods and return proper status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Good documentation helps other developers understand how to use the API without confusion. Versioning is also important, because it allows you to update your API without breaking existing applications. By following these practices, you can build APIs that are reliable, consistent, and simple for others to integrate into their own projects.
